title: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's
body:
Read the chapter → [Deuteronomy 3](/bible/deuteronomy/3)

## Introduction

This session covered Deuteronomy 3-6. As Israel nears the end of the first five books, the thread of each is worth holding: Genesis is the beginning, the book of your genes and genealogy; Exodus is the grand exit from slavery in Egypt; Leviticus carries the levitical laws given through the Levites; Numbers is the numbering of the families and armies of Israel; and Deuteronomy is a reiteration, a repetition of the laws of the Most High and of everything that happened in the previous books. Chapters 1 and 2 retold how the Most High helped Moses by appointing leaders, so that one man would not carry the whole burden of a stiffnecked and rebellious people alone, and gave Israel instruction on which wars to take on, sparing Edom and the children of Moab. Chapter 3 opens with the war against Og king of Bashan.

**[Deuteronomy 3:1-3](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v1)</sup> Then we turned, and went up the way to Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v2)</sup> And the Lord said unto me, Fear him not: for I will deliver him, and all his people, and his land, into thy hand; and thou shalt do unto him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v3)</sup> So the Lord our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining.

- Bashan is about to be conquered, and Og the king of Bashan came out with all his people to battle at Edrei. The Most High said fear him not, for I will deliver him and all his people and his land into thy hand, as was done to Sihon king of the Amorites at Heshbon.
- Always remember, the battle is the Lord's; this fight is spiritual. Israel does not need weapons of mass destruction: the Bible is the weapon, and when Israel keeps the commandments the Most High fights for his people.
- The Lord our God delivered into our hands also the king of Bashan: they were out there doing physical war, but they gave the praise, the glory, and the victory to the Most High. They did not boast in their own swords; that is how you sanctify the Most High.
- The same order stands today: when you wake up you thank the Most High, and you thank him for the food even though you cooked it, because he is the one who allowed you to have it. You always put the Most High first.

**[Deuteronomy 3:4-7](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v4)</sup> And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v5)</sup> All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v6)</sup> And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v7)</sup> But all the cattle, and the spoil of the cities, we took for a prey to ourselves.

- Threescore cities were taken, all fenced with high walls, gates, and bars, beside unwalled towns a great many, and not one city was left untaken.
- They utterly destroyed the men, women, and children of every city, as they did unto Sihon king of Heshbon. That command came from the Most High himself; this is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of the Bible, not the invented gospel that says he loves everybody no matter what.
- Only the cattle and the spoil of the cities were taken for a prey; those were needed and were spared.

**[Deuteronomy 3:8-11](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v8)</sup> And we took at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites the land that was on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon;
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v9)</sup> (Which Hermon the Sidonians call Sirion; and the Amorites call it Shenir;)
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v10)</sup> All the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, unto Salchah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v11)</sup> For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.

- Israel took the land from the two kings of the Amorites on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon.
- Only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants. His bedstead was a bedstead of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits broad: about thirteen feet long and six feet wide, near the size of two king beds, showing how tall and big this man was.
- Og was an Amorite, and the Amorites descend from Ham; [Genesis 10](/bible/genesis/10) proves the lineage. The Hamitic nations were known for great stature, as Goliath the Philistine stood nine feet nine inches, and to this day the tallest peoples on earth, the Watusi, the Dinka, and the Nilotic tribes of Sudan, Ethiopia, and Kenya, are Hamites.
- Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 10:5](/bible/genesis/10#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/genesis/10#v5)</sup> By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.

    The Most High divided the isles of the Gentiles, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations; the nations were never the same, he divided them by tongue and land.
  - **[Genesis 10:6](/bible/genesis/10#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/genesis/10#v6)</sup> And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.

    The sons of Ham: Cush is Ethiopia, Mizraim is Egypt, with Phut and Canaan; Ham, the youngest son of Noah, is the progenitor of these dark nations, and Kemet and Ham mean the same thing.
  - **[Genesis 10:16](/bible/genesis/10#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/genesis/10#v16)</sup> And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite,

    The Jebusite and the Amorite are of the lineage of Canaan; the Amorites are a Hamitic tribe, so Og the Amorite descends from Ham.

**[Deuteronomy 3:12-17](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v12)</sup> And this land, which we possessed at that time, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, and half mount Gilead, and the cities thereof, gave I unto the Reubenites and to the Gadites.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v13)</sup> And the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, being the kingdom of Og, gave I unto the half tribe of Manasseh; all the region of Argob, with all Bashan, which was called the land of giants.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v14)</sup> Jair the son of Manasseh took all the country of Argob unto the coasts of Geshuri and Maachathi; and called them after his own name, Bashan–havoth–jair, unto this day.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v15)</sup> And I gave Gilead unto Machir.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v16)</sup> And unto the Reubenites and unto the Gadites I gave from Gilead even unto the river Arnon half the valley, and the border even unto the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v17)</sup> The plain also, and Jordan, and the coast thereof, from Chinnereth even unto the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, under Ashdoth–pisgah eastward.

- The conquered land was divided: from Aroer by the river Arnon and half mount Gilead to the Reubenites and the Gadites, and the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, to the half tribe of Manasseh.
- All the region of Argob with all Bashan was called the land of giants, because the giants there were of Og's kin, of his family.
- Jair the son of Manasseh took all the country of Argob and called it after his own name, Bashan-havoth-jair, unto this day.

**[Deuteronomy 3:18-20](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v18)</sup> And I commanded you at that time, saying, The Lord your God hath given you this land to possess it: ye shall pass over armed before your brethren the children of Israel, all that are meet for the war.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v19)</sup> But your wives, and your little ones, and your cattle, (for I know that ye have much cattle,) shall abide in your cities which I have given you;
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v20)</sup> Until the Lord have given rest unto your brethren, as well as unto you, and until they also possess the land which the Lord your God hath given them beyond Jordan: and then shall ye return every man unto his possession, which I have given you.

- All that were meet for the war were to pass over armed before their brethren, while the wives, the little ones, and the much cattle abode in the cities already given, until the Most High gave rest to their brethren and they also possessed their land beyond Jordan.
- When you read these wars, put yourself in the position of the brothers going out. Being promised victory over the land did not mean every man would survive it; Israel still had casualties, and there were brothers that gave their lives for their people.
- Read to understand, not just to say you read your four chapters: bring the scripture to life and visualize what was really going on.

**[Deuteronomy 3:21-22](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v21)</sup> And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, Thine eyes have seen all that the Lord your God hath done unto these two kings: so shall the Lord do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v22)</sup> Ye shall not fear them: for the Lord your God he shall fight for you.

- Joshua was commanded at that time: thine eyes have seen all that the Lord your God hath done unto these two kings; so shall he do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest.
- Ye shall not fear them, for the Lord your God he shall fight for you; the victories over Sihon and Og were the proof set before Joshua's own eyes.

**[Deuteronomy 3:23-24](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v23)</sup> And I besought the Lord at that time, saying,
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v24)</sup> O Lord God, thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness, and thy mighty hand: for what God is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy works, and according to thy might?

- Moses besought the Most High: thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness and thy mighty hand, for what God is there in heaven or in earth that can do according to thy works and according to thy might?
- That greatness shown to Moses was more than the exodus. On Sinai he received the ten commandments and the six hundred plus commandments, ceremonial, civil, moral, dietary, and sacrificial, that the Most High ordained Israel to keep.
- He was also told many wondrous things: the prophecies such as [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), that the people would go into slave ships under yokes of iron, lose their nationality, become a byword and an astonishment, and that a small remnant would wake up in the end days and come back.
- He was shown the secrets of the times, the understanding of the parables and allegories of the scriptures, and the end itself; all of that stands behind this thanksgiving in Deuteronomy.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Esdras 14:3-6](/bible/2-esdras/14#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/2-esdras/14#v3)</sup> Then said he unto me, In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt:
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/2-esdras/14#v4)</sup> And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season,
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/2-esdras/14#v5)</sup> And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end; and commanded him, saying,
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/2-esdras/14#v6)</sup> These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.

    The Most High held Moses by him a long season, told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times and the end; that is the greatness and the mighty hand Moses praised.

**[Deuteronomy 3:25-26](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v25)**

> <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v25)</sup> I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v26)</sup> But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me: and the Lord said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter.

- Moses begged: I pray thee, let me go over and see the good land that is beyond Jordan. The Most High had already told him he would not see the promised land, and Moses was trying to get him to repent of the word he had given.
- The sentence came from the water of Meribah: Moses said hear now, ye rebels, must we fetch you water out of this rock, and smote the rock twice. He took the credit and became high minded instead of sanctifying the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, so he was told he would not bring the congregation into the land.
- The contrast is [Deuteronomy 3:3](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v3): after the war with Og the people said the Lord our God delivered them into our hands. That is sanctifying the Most High; Moses at the rock did the opposite.
- The Lord was wroth with me for your sakes: Moses laid it on stiffnecked Israel. And the answer was final, let it suffice thee, speak no more unto me of this matter, as a parent tells a child that keeps begging that the matter is closed and had better not be raised again.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 20:10-12](/bible/numbers/20#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/numbers/20#v10)</sup> And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/numbers/20#v11)</sup> And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/numbers/20#v12)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.

    Moses smote the rock twice and the water came out abundantly, but because he believed not, to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, he and Aaron would not bring the congregation into the land.

**[Deuteronomy 3:27-29](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v27)**

> <sup>[27](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v27)</sup> Get thee up into the top of Pisgah, and lift up thine eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and behold it with thine eyes: for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v28)</sup> But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him: for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which thou shalt see.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v29)</sup> So we abode in the valley over against Beth–peor.

- Get thee up into the top of Pisgah and behold the land with thine eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, for thou shalt not go over this Jordan; seeing it from the mountain was all that was granted.
- But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people and cause them to inherit the land. The Most High said plainly whom he would deal with for the crossing.
- Promotion comes from the Most High: he was dealing with Moses and declared who he wanted in charge, and Moses was to strengthen the man chosen to replace him.
